title: Ambient diagonal purity and its normalized base-change map
statement:
Let $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ with $\ell$ prime [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $Y$ be an excellent Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible and $h:X\to Y$ a separated smooth morphism of finite type and pure relative dimension $r\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings; excellence is [def-exc-excellent-ring]. On ordinary unbounded etale $A$-module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and its ambient right adjoint $h^\times$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Put $\omega_h=h^\times A_Y$. Define $A_T(1)=\mu_{\ell^m,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^m}A$ for any $m$ with $\ell^mA=0$, its tensor powers $A_T(r)$, and $M(r)=M\otimes_A^LA_T(r)$; these definitions are independent of $m$.

The diagonal-class/deformation-to-the-normal-bundle construction gives an orientation $a_h:A_X(r)[2r]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$. More precisely its inverse is the diagonal restriction $\omega_h\cong\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}$, followed by deformation of the diagonal section to the zero section of $T_{X/Y}$, followed by restriction of the inverse Kummer-normalized vector-bundle purity map. Here $p_1:X\times_YX\to X$ and $\Delta:X\to X\times_YX$. For every $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the tensor map defined as the $Rh_!\dashv h^\times$ transpose of inverse projection followed by the counit gives a natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_h(M):h^*M(r)[2r]\xrightarrow{\sim}h^\times M.$$
There is no boundedness, constructibility or finite-Tor hypothesis on $M$.

For a Cartesian base change $v:Y'\to Y$ with $Y'$ excellent Noetherian, let $u:X'\to X$, $h':X'\to Y'$ be its projections and $B:v^*Rh_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh'_!u^*$ compact-support base change. The canonical exceptional comparison $c_M:u^*h^\times M\to h'^\times v^*M$ is the transpose of $v^*\epsilon_h(M)\circ B^{-1}$. Under canonical pullback and twist identifications,
$$c_M\circ u^*\gamma_h(M)=\gamma_{h'}(v^*M).$$
The orientations, tensor maps and adjoint smooth traces therefore commute with this base change and composition; for $r=0$ they are the etale adjunction maps. This includes base change to separably closed fields, arbitrary extensions of such fields, and geometric fibres of excellent traits.

For all $L,M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the exceptional internal-Hom comparison
$$H_h:h^\times R\mathcal Hom_A(L,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(h^*L,h^\times M)$$
is an isomorphism. It is specified by the pairing $h^\times R\mathcal Hom_A(L,M)\otimes h^*L\to h^\times(R\mathcal Hom_A(L,M)\otimes L)\to h^\times M$, where the first arrow is the counit-defined exceptional tensor map and the second is evaluation. Internal Hom and tensor have their ordinary unbounded meanings [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-kun-derived-tensor]. This specifies the evaluation normalization of the isomorphism as well as its direction.

source.place: Finite-stage argument with arbitrary finite coefficients; sk-prop-sp-orientation.proof.md (diagonal, deformation, vector bundle), sk-prop-sp-purity-bc-factors.md. Agent extension to the ordinary ambient excellent-Noetherian setting, retaining the lecture-notes route; Scholze, Six-Functor Formalisms, Lecture V, Theorem 5.5 and its base-change conclusion.

proof.text: Choose $m\geq1$ with $\ell^mA=0$. The finite Tate-sheaf lemma gives the independence of $m$, local freeness of rank one and every pullback/tensor identification used below. Finite-type permanence makes $X$, $X\times_YX$ and the base-changed schemes Noetherian. A Noetherian base is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so Nagata supplies compactifications of the separated finite-type maps in the argument. The permanence of smooth relative dimension gives the dimensions of their base changes and composites. Therefore the ambient compact-support adjunctions and their unbounded composition and base-change comparisons apply, including to $p_1$ and to the vector-bundle and deformation maps of the section lemma. Set $\omega_b=b^\times A$.

source.place: Finite-stage argument; verification of the ordinary Noetherian ambient hypotheses

proof.text:
Apply ambient smooth exceptional base change at $A_Y$ to the Cartesian self-base-change square of $h$. It gives $b:p_2^*\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_1}$. Since $p_2\Delta=1_X$, its pullback gives $j_h:\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}$. The diagonal is a regular closed immersion of codimension $r$ with normal bundle $T_{X/Y}$. Apply the finite-ring section-deformation lemma to $(p_1,\Delta)$, obtaining $\delta_h:\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi$, where $\pi:T_{X/Y}\to X$ and $z$ is zero. Vector-bundle purity at $A_X$ gives $v_\pi:A_{T_{X/Y}}(r)[2r]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_\pi$. Define
$$\theta_h=z^*(v_\pi^{-1})\circ\delta_h\circ j_h:\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(r)[2r],\qquad a_h=\theta_h^{-1}.$$
Every arrow has now been specified by the diagonal/deformation construction of the statement.

source.place: Orientation proof: diagonal, deformation and inverse vector-bundle purity

proof.text: Let $\phi_h(M):h^*M\otimes\omega_h\to h^\times M$ be the transpose of inverse projection followed by $1\otimes\epsilon_h(A_Y)$. The ambient smooth-tensor theorem says exactly that this map is an isomorphism for every $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Define $\gamma_h(M)=\phi_h(M)\circ(1\otimes a_h)$, inserting the tensor/shift reassociation. Naturality follows from the naturality of $\phi_h$ and tensor. This proves the claimed unbounded purity formula without imposing a condition on $M$.

source.place: Finite-stage proof: orientation followed by the canonical tensor map

proof.text:
For the base change $(u,v)$ of the question, put $b_h=c_{A_Y}:u^*\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{h'}$. The ambient smooth base-change theorem specifies this as the transpose of the pulled-back counit through compact-support exchange, exactly the specified $c_M$. It also gives, for every unbounded $M$,
$$c_M\circ u^*\phi_h(M)=\phi_{h'}(v^*M)\circ(1\otimes b_h).$$
Its hypotheses require a finite ring annihilated by an invertible integer, Noetherian schemes and smooth compactifiable $h$; Step 1 verified these. No finite-type assumption on $v$ is used.

source.place: Base-change factors (2): equality of the actual tensor maps

proof.text: The self-product square for $h'$ is the pullback of that for $h$. Coherent exceptional mates of compact-support exchange identify their maps $j_h$: pull back $p_2^*\omega_h\to\omega_{p_1}$ and then restrict along the base-changed diagonal. The two possible orders agree by mate pasting and compatibility of unbounded compact-support exchange with composition. The section-deformation lemma identifies $u^*\delta_h$ with $\delta_{h'}$ under these same exceptional comparisons, including the normal-bundle comparison. Thus the first two factors of $\theta_h$ commute with this base change.

source.place: Deformation and base-change factors (1), first two orientation factors

proof.text:
For the last factor, locally trivialize $T_{X/Y}$. Vector-bundle integration is the specified affine-space counit on each trivializing open, and that counit commutes with arbitrary Noetherian base change. Consequently the two integration maps agree on the pulled-back cover. This is an equality of maps between objects concentrated in degree zero: locally both compact-support coefficient objects are isomorphic to $A$. Full faithfulness of the degree-zero embedding and sheaf-Hom gluing therefore give equality globally. Taking exceptional mates yields the same assertion for $v_\pi$ and then for $z^*(v_\pi^{-1})$. Together with Step 5 this is
$$\theta_{h'}b_h=u^*\theta_h,\qquad b_h\,u^*a_h=a_{h'}.$$
Substitute the latter equality into Step 4 to obtain $c_Mu^*\gamma_h(M)=\gamma_{h'}(v^*M)$. Taking compact-support adjuncts proves the corresponding assertion for the smooth traces.

source.place: Base-change factors (1), vector-bundle factor and the final equality

proof.text: Here is the local normalization needed for composition. Choose a smooth coordinate chart $e:U\to\mathbf A^r_V$ for $h$, with $U,V$ affine opens. On $U\times_VU$, the functions $e_j(x_2)-e_j(x_1)$ are etale coordinates for $p_1$ near the diagonal. Remove the other components of their zero locus, as in the section-deformation lemma. That lemma identifies $\delta_h$ with the identity of the standard section line in these coordinates. Its normal-bundle identification is the differential of $e$. Linear invariance of vector-bundle integration and its affine-space normalization identify the third factor with the affine-space orientation. The base-change map $j_h$ is computed through the etale chart $w'=(x_1,e(x_2))$ to $\mathbf A^r_U$, which carries $\Delta$ to the section $\sigma=(x,e(x))$, whereas the section lemma uses $w=(x_1,e(x_2)-e(x_1))=\tau_{\sigma}\circ w'$, carrying $\Delta$ to zero; here $\tau_\sigma$ is translation by $-e(x_1)$ on $\mathbf A^r_U\to U$. By the ambient translation lemma over the Noetherian base $U$, $\tau_\sigma$ preserves the coordinate-tower trace of $\mathbf A^r_U$, so by mate pasting the trivializations of $\omega_{p_1}$ obtained through $w$ and through $w'$ agree; this replaces the translation step of the vector-bundle orientation proof. The self-product squares for the coordinate factorization $h=p_re$ paste to the self-product square for $h$; mate pasting identifies $j_h$ with the etale restriction of the corresponding affine-space map. Hence $a_h|_U$ is the pullback of the ordered affine-space orientation through $e$, under the canonical etale comparison $e^*p_r^\times\cong( p_re)^\times$. The tensor-mate identity for etale precomposition identifies $\gamma_h(M)|_U$ with the same coordinate adjunction at every $M$. This calculation uses the finite-ring section lemma, rather than a fixed-field orientation theorem.

source.place: Deformation coordinate normalization; orientation-charts proof Steps 1–4; translation: sk-prop-sp-orientation/sk-prop-sp-orientation-vector-bundle.proof.md, Step 1

proof.text:
Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be composable morphisms satisfying the smooth hypotheses, of dimensions $d,e$. Write $q_{g,f}:(gf)^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}f^\times g^\times$ for the adjunction comparison. The projection-composition identity and the composite counit $\epsilon_g\circ Rg_!\epsilon_f$ give, on taking transposes,
$$\phi_{gf}(M)\circ(1\otimes s_{f,g})=q_{g,f}^{-1}\circ f^\times\phi_g(M)\circ\phi_f(g^*M\otimes\omega_g),$$
where $s_{f,g}=q_{g,f}^{-1}\circ\phi_f(\omega_g): f^*\omega_g\otimes\omega_f\to\omega_{gf}$, and the source on the left is $(gf)^*M\otimes f^*\omega_g\otimes\omega_f$. To see the equality, apply $R(gf)_!$ and the counit: replace its projection by the successive $f$ and $g$ projections, and replace its counit by the displayed composite counit. The two resulting maps are then the identical successive projection-and-counit composite. This proves the formal tensor part of composition.

source.place: Composition proof Step 2: explicit projection-and-counit transpose calculation

proof.text:
Choose compatible affine smooth charts $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$ for $f$ and $V\to\mathbf A^e_W$ for $g$. Their composite chart is etale over $\mathbf A^{d+e}_W$, ordered with the $d$ fibre coordinates before the $e$ base coordinates. Step 7 identifies the diagonal orientations with those chart orientations. The coordinate-tower adjunction in the affine-space trace lemma is defined by successively composing affine-line adjunctions. The tower with $d+e$ coordinates and the successive towers with $d$ and $e$ coordinates therefore have the same composite counit, with the unbounded compact-support composition comparisons inserted. Etale precomposition preserves those counits; mate pasting identifies their right-adjoint comparisons. Thus, on this cover,
$$a_{gf}=s_{f,g}\circ(f^*a_g\otimes a_f).$$
Both sides are maps between equal shifts of rank-one locally constant sheaves by smooth tensor. Equality is consequently a sheaf-map equality, so full faithfulness and sheaf-Hom gluing give it globally. Step 8 now gives composition for every $\gamma(M)$; taking adjuncts gives trace composition. The twist shifts $2d,2e$ are even, so interchanging them introduces no sign.

source.place: Composition proof Step 1: coordinate-tower comparison and global sheaf equality

proof.text: For $r=0$, the section and rank-zero vector-bundle factors in Step 2 are identities on the standard pairs. The etale proper-support comparison identifies compact-support direct image with exact sum extension, preserving its sum counit. The etale locality adjunction identifies its right adjoint with $h^*$. Under this identification $a_h$ is the identity at $A$, and the tensor-mate computation identifies $\gamma_h(M)$ with the right-adjoint comparison preserving that sum counit. Its adjunct is therefore the etale sum/evaluation counit. In fact Steps 1–9 only used Noetherianity of the bases, not excellence. They therefore apply to the indicated geometric-field extensions and geometric fibres: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal. The base-change maps need not be of finite type.

source.place: Dimension-zero normalization and the indicated changes of base

proof.text:
Finally, the proper projection formula and the open extension tensor identity give the compact-support projection isomorphism $Rh_!(T\otimes h^*L)\cong Rh_!T\otimes L$ for all unbounded $T,L$. Use the ambient adjunction and the closed tensor--Hom adjunction to obtain, naturally in every test object $T$ on $X$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,h^\times R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rh_!T,R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rh_!T\otimes L,M)$$
$$\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rh_!(T\otimes h^*L),M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes h^*L,h^\times M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,R\mathcal Hom(h^*L,h^\times M)).$$
This chain of bijections shows that its representing comparison is an isomorphism (apply its inverse to the identity of the target to construct a two-sided inverse). There is no dualizability assumption on $L$.

source.place: Exceptional internal-Hom comparison: formal unbounded projection adjunction

proof.text:
To check the direction and normalization of this comparison, put $Q=R\mathcal Hom(L,M)$ and take $T=h^\times Q$ and the identity as the initial morphism in Step 11. Before the last tensor--Hom transpose its image is the exceptional adjunct of
$$Rh_!(h^\times Q\otimes h^*L)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}Rh_!h^\times Q\otimes L\xrightarrow{\epsilon_Q\otimes1}Q\otimes L\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}}M.$$
The exceptional tensor map in the statement is defined by exactly the first two arrows as an adjunct, with target $h^\times(Q\otimes L)$. Composing that adjunct with $h^\times\operatorname{ev}$ therefore gives the pairing in the question. Its tensor--Hom transpose is the isomorphism of Step 11, so it is precisely $H_h$ in the required direction.
